quote.text: A healthy pair of eyes should see everything that can be seen and not say, “No! Too bright!” (which is a symptom of ophthalmia). A healthy sense of hearing or smell should be prepared for any sound or scent; a healthy stomach should have the same reaction to all foods, as a mill to what it grinds. So too a healthy mind should be prepared for anything. The one that keeps saying, “Are my children all right?” or “Everyone must approve of me” is like eyes that can only stand pale colors, or teeth that can handle only mush.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Embrace your children’s natural development as you would a healthy mind—ready to face all experiences without overreacting to every setback or success.
    • Let go of the constant need for external validation (“Are my children all right?”) and trust in the innate capacity of your children to grow resiliently when nurtured with balanced guidance.
  • Leadership
    • Like eyes that see without flinching at brightness, good leaders absorb both praise and criticism with equal measure, understanding that every observation is an opportunity for growth.
    • Steer clear of the trap of seeking universal approval; instead, focus on steadfast decision-making and self-assurance inspired by an inner clarity that withstands external noise.
  • Product Management
    • Adopt the mindset of a healthy stomach that processes all kinds of foods—be ready for a flood of diverse ideas, feedback, and market trends, accepting them without bias.
    • View challenges and iterations in your product development like a mill grinding any raw material; each input, no matter how unrefined, is essential for creating a refined, resilient final product.
